contributed_sources.description: Batty and Bridson, Accurate Viscous Free Surfaces for Buckling Coiling and Rotating Liquids, 2008.
contributed_sources.inspection: Full original text inspected, especially sections 3–5. Coupled symmetric-gradient viscosity, free-surface traction, variational dissipation, rigid-rotation counterexample.

contributed_sources.description: Brackbill, Kothe, and Zemach, A Continuum Method for Modeling Surface Tension, JCP 100, 335–354, 1992.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original-paper text surfaced through academic-hosted PDF. Continuum surface force and wall adhesion boundary treatment. DOI 10.1016/0021-9991(92)90240-Y.

contributed_sources.description: Young, An Essay on the Cohesion of Fluids, 1805.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original archival metadata verified; the journal DOI endpoint returned 403. Used only for historical attribution of material-dependent contact angle, not to attribute modern notation verbatim. DOI 10.1098/rstl.1805.0005.

contributed_sources.description: Huh and Scriven, Hydrodynamic Model of Steady Movement of a Solid Liquid Fluid Contact Line, 1971.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original abstract inspected. Creeping-flow contact-line stress/dissipation singularity under adherence. DOI 10.1016/0021-9797(71)90188-3.

contributed_sources.description: Cox, The Dynamics of the Spreading of Liquids on a Solid Surface Part 1 Viscous Flow, JFM 168, 169–194, 1986.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original abstract and bibliographic details inspected. Small-Ca matched-asymptotic/slip assumptions verified. Full publisher text was not retrieved; do not present the cubic shorthand as its general finite-angle equation. DOI 10.1017/S0022112086000332.

contributed_sources.description: Qian, Wang, and Sheng, Molecular Scale Contact Line Hydrodynamics of Immiscible Flows, PRE 68, 016306, 2003.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original full text inspected. Generalized Navier boundary condition, Cahn–Hilliard framework, molecular comparison and fitted dynamic parameters. DOI 10.1103/PhysRevE.68.016306.

contributed_sources.description: Batty, Bertails, and Bridson, A Fast Variational Framework for Accurate Solid Fluid Coupling, 2007.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original project, paper text, and sample-code descriptions inspected. Kinetic projection, static irregular-boundary samples, and author hindsight on improved weights. Sample archive license not verified.

contributed_sources.description: Popinet, An Accurate Adaptive Solver for Surface Tension Driven Interfacial Flows, JCP 228, 5838–5866, 2009.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original publisher abstract/conclusion inspected. Balanced-force VOF with height-function curvature and stationary-drop equilibrium. Author PDF endpoint timed out. DOI 10.1016/j.jcp.2009.04.042.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original contact-angle implementation.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source and explicit limitations inspected. Height-function normal fallback and shallow-angle limitation are visible in the implementation.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original surface-tension implementation.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source inspected. Explicit capillary timestep restriction and curvature potential construction.

contributed_sources.description: Akinci, Akinci, and Teschner, Versatile Surface Tension and Adhesion for SPH Fluids, TOG 32(6), 2013.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original text inspected. Cohesion and boundary attraction as practical SPH models. DOI 10.1145/2508363.2508395.

contributed_sources.description: Weiler, Koschier, Brand, and Bender, A Physically Consistent Implicit Viscosity Solver for SPH Fluids, CGF 37(2), 2018.
contributed_sources.inspection: Author abstract and accepted-paper text inspected. Conservation, refinement, and spurious-viscosity evaluation criteria.

contributed_sources.description: Bender et al., Implicit Frictional Boundary Handling for SPH.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original manuscript passages inspected. Boundary viscosity/friction extension and separate boundary coefficient. Filename uses 2020; final issue metadata was not verified.

contributed_sources.description: SPlisHSPlasH Weiler2018 implementation.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source inspection confirms μ = configured viscosity × rest density and separate boundary coefficient. No build/execution.

contributed_sources.description: Macklin and Müller, Position Based Fluids, 2013.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original algorithm inspected. Positional density constraints, artificial pressure, velocity postprocessing, and performance/accuracy tradeoff.

contributed_sources.description: Koschier and Bender, Density Maps for Improved SPH Boundary Handling, SCA 2017.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original author abstract inspected. Precomputed continuous boundary density contribution.

contributed_sources.description: Bender, Kugelstadt, Weiler, and Koschier, Volume Maps An Implicit Boundary Representation for SPH, MIG 2019.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original text inspected. Kernel-independent geometric-volume contribution, rigid boundaries, comparison with density maps.

contributed_sources.description: Guendelman, Selle, Losasso, and Fedkiw, Coupling Water and Smoke to Thin Deformable and Rigid Shells, SIGGRAPH 2005.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original abstract and paper passages inspected. Infinitesimally thin surfaces, ray-based visibility, and incompressibility treatment.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original embedded-boundary implementation.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source inspected. Volume/face geometry, small-cell CFL restriction, tracer redistribution. Static implementation details are not asserted to establish arbitrary moving-boundary correctness.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk core license text.
contributed_sources.inspection: GPL version 3 text verified. Per-file scope and downstream compatibility still require checking.

contributed_sources.description: SPlisHSPlasH repository license.
contributed_sources.inspection: MIT notice verified. Repository README separately warns that dependencies have their own terms.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original 2D sessile-drop test.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source and analytic geometry comparison inspected. The implementation tests 15°–165° and notes shallower limitations.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original 3D sessile-drop test.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original source inspected as the 3D comparison. No local reproduction performed.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original parasitic-current test.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source inspected. Constant density, diameter 0.8, Laplace-number-controlled viscosity, viscous-time observation, resolution study.

contributed_sources.description: Basilisk original drop-oscillation test.
contributed_sources.inspection: Source/diagnostics inspected. Frequency error and equivalent numerical viscosity are separate quantities. Its dimensional setup must be retained when reproducing it.

contributed_sources.description: Washburn, The Dynamics of Capillary Flow, Physical Review 17, 273–283, 1921.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original abstract inspected. Cylindrical-capillary square-root penetration formula. Full text is access controlled; no access bypass attempted.

contributed_sources.description: Gong et al., Contactless Surface Tension Measurement of Molten Oxides Using Oscillating Drop Method in an Aerodynamic Levitator.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original measurement equations and experimental cautions inspected. Supports Rayleigh frequency convention and the need to control external forcing, mode splitting, and rotation. No material values imported as Rheon presets.

contributed_sources.description: François, Cummins, Dendy, Kothe, Sicilian, and Williams, A Balanced Force Algorithm for Continuous and Sharp Interfacial Surface Tension Models within a Volume Tracking Framework, JCP 213, 141–173, 2006.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original author-uploaded text inspected; publisher endpoint failed. Exact-curvature balanced-force experiment is an appropriate control before testing estimated curvature. DOI 10.1016/j.jcp.2005.08.004.

contributed_sources.description: SPlisHSPlasH Akinci2013 implementation.
contributed_sources.inspection: Original source inspected. Separate fluid and boundary force coefficients, with boundary-method branches. No assumption that every branch reproduces every original-paper conservation claim.
